name: doctor-worktree-realpath-false-warn
title: Doctor global-core-realpath falsely warns in linked worktrees, blowing the brief byte budget and blocking every worktree DONE
description: Environmental regression found while closing B-3b05 on 2026-07-14: the doctor global-core-realpath check warns whenever lattice runs inside a linked worktree, because the global @lattice/core realpath resolves to the repo canonical main checkout (/packages/main) while the check expects the CURRENT project root (.worktrees/B-xxxx/packages/main). That resolution is the documented, expected deployment (global CLI = canonical main dist; worktrees are never relinked per-worktree), so the warn plus its repair block (Relink or reinstall the global @lattice/core package) is a false positive in every worktree. Concrete damage: the warn adds ~240 bytes to doctor brief output, pushing it to 20239 bytes against the 20000-byte budget asserted by brief-output-smoke (packages/main/dist/tasks/brief-output-smoke.js, from B-7c05); npm test is in the DONE-required command set (done_required_validate: FAIL root full test suite), so done_prepare validate hard-blocks DONE for EVERY in-flight worktree story (reproduced on B-3b05; main checkout passes the same suite, proving the failure is location-dependent, not story code). Fix direction: make the global-core-realpath check worktree-aware — when cwd is a linked worktree of the same repository and the global realpath equals that repository canonical main checkout packages/main, classify as pass/info with no repair block (brief stays under budget); keep the genuine mismatch warn (global resolving to an unrelated path) intact with a regression test for both contexts. Raising the smoke byte budget instead would hide the false warn and is not the fix.
